goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weed check` judges a diff and may block; `weed scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weed guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weed bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop. Make the checks below pass, honestly.
Nobody reviews your prose, only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
Before weed is allowed to block anyone, it runs over real history: `weed check --base <parent> --strict` on up to the last 200 commits of the default branch in tilth, pleach, tend2, copeca and umbel. `docs/calibration-2026-09.md` records per repo the commits judged, blocked and warned, and classifies every blocked commit as true positive, acceptable, or false positive. The ship bar is block-level false positives under two percent of the pooled commits across the five repos, with per-repo counts shown; a repo with fewer than 50 commits is reported, not judged alone. The kill bar is reaching that bar only by disabling T1, T2, T3 or S1; then the verdict is written in the file's first sentence and weed does not ship as a gate. The metric command `garden.json` names is this measurement.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/calibration.tend2.html) is your full context, read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) `cargo xtask calibrate` judges up to the last 200 commits of each listed repo against their parents, writes `docs/calibration-2026-09.md` in the described shape with the verdict first, and leaves the source repositories untouched · evidence expected at: scripts/check/calibrate.sh
- (code) the calibration file's pooled block-level false-positive share is under two percent of commits judged across the repos, every repo's own count and share is shown, and no line of it records T1, T2, T3 or S1 turned off to get there · evidence expected at: scripts/check/calibration-bar.sh
- (code) `garden.json`'s metric command runs `scripts/check/calibration-bar.sh` and its latest result is committed · evidence expected at: scripts/check/metric.sh
- (code) `cargo xtask suppressions` counts `Weed-allow:` trailers per hundred commits on each garden repo from the day guard is installed (zero before), and the calibration file reports the rate beside precision with the true-positive count on the same line · evidence expected at: scripts/check/suppression-rate.sh

## Definition of done, verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/calibration.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload 1700f20ebe72 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

## Already tried (do not repeat)
- 2026-09-05 repos follow the umbrella loop's list; the brief's rctrl is umbel's former name and the same repository
- 2026-09-05 `xtask` over a script so the calibration runs the same core the binary ships, with no second implementation of the diff walk
- 2026-09-05 bar refined on the channel by cape-town: the two percent applies to the pooled total across repos, with per-repo counts shown; a repo under 50 commits is reported, not judged alone
- 2026-09-05 cape-town: track the suppression rate from the day guard is installed and report it beside precision; rising suppressions with flat true positives means the gate is gamed or mis-tuned. The recall section of the same file belongs to the recall loop, and the second party's classification to calibration-audit
- 2026-09-05 cape-town's ruling on specimens: `weed.toml` may exclude paths only under `fixtures/adversarial/**` (and the specimen directories a repo names), every excluded path is still reported at note level in the SARIF so an exclusion is as visible as an allowance, and it is a list of directories, never a rule toggle. This is what lets `weed check` on weed's own tree report nothing at block level, and it lands with calibration

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file, check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green, it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Probe/scratch files (toolchain checks, experiments) go in `.loop-scratch/` only, it is never collected; scratch files elsewhere pollute the delivery.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root, what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
